title: Streamline regional route resolution and consolidate fallback decision paths
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Background: The smart routing layer has accrued several incremental fixes to support region affinity, capacity-aware fallbacks, and legacy policy adapters. These fixes reduced immediate incidents but increased code complexity: redundant route evaluations, duplicated fallback heuristics per-region, and lock-heavy state mutation paths. This ticket consolidates those responsibilities into a compact evaluation pipeline to reduce p99 request latency and lower CPU contention under high fanout. Goal: 1) Replace ad-hoc per-region fallback logic with a single compact fallback coordinator that reasons about capacity, latency SLO, and model compatibility. 2) Extract a lightweight RouteContext struct that owns only the evaluation snapshot (immutable during a request) so downstream adapters are lock-free. 3) Remove two legacy policy adapters and replace them with policy adapters implemented against the new small interface. 4) Add targeted observability (trace spans + cardinality-limited tags) so we can debug fallback paths without high metric cardinality. Non-goal: full rewrite of policy DSL or changing policy semantics beyond behavior-preserving simplifications. Success criteria: - p99 latency of routing decision path reduced by >= 12% on medium-size requests (baseline attached). - CPU work per routing request reduced by >= 20% under 1000 RPS synthetic test. - No customer-visible behavioral regressions in staged canary (rollout gating tests pass). - Reduced lock hold-time measured via runtime latency spans. See design doc and perf harness: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Compact+Fallback+Coordinator+Design Perf harness + load tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-perf/tree/eng/compact-fallback
updates: 2026-03-06: Spike complete — prototyped RouteContext snapshot that copies only the minimal fields (region, model set, token budget, route priorities). Verified memory footprint is < 1.5KB per request in Go runtime (profiler: heap/alloc).

2026-03-07: Design review with PM and Runtime team. Decision: keep policy semantics identical; implement transformation layer to translate old adapter outputs into new decision objects to avoid cascading changes. Action: create compatibility shim (ENG-47912) for 2-week deprecation window.

2026-03-09: Benchmarked current master vs prototype on a 16-core routing-worker. Baseline p99: 14.8ms. Prototype p99: 12.9ms (13% improvement). CPU cycles per op reduced ~18% on median. Attaching perf logs in the PR. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4123

2026-03-11: Implemented compact fallback coordinator logic and unit tests. Coordinator evaluates candidate pools in a prioritized order, applies soft-threshold capacity checks, and emits a deterministic fallback reason code for observability. Added deterministic tie-breaker to maintain reproducibility for replay tests.

2026-03-12: Integration tests failing intermittently in multi-region simulation: observed stale capacity snapshot leading to suboptimal fallbacks under bursty load. Mitigation: move to compare-on-read semantics for short-lived counters and add an optimistic concurrency retry with bounded attempts. Patch submitted (PR 4137).

2026-03-13: Code review completed for coordinator and RouteContext (2 approvals from runtime owners). Noted follow-ups: - Add metric for fallback_decision_latency_ms - Reduce tag cardinality on region-level traces - Add canary configs for 10% traffic in us-east-1

2026-03-14: Rolling deploy to staging routing cluster (canary 5% in us-east-1). Running synthetic customer workloads. Observability dashboards created: routing/compact-fallbacks (Grafana) and traces surfaced in Tempo. Early results: no increase in error rate; p95 routing latency stable; awaiting p99 numbers after 24h window.
comments: Marco Rivera (2026-03-09): Left inline review on coordinator loop — prefer early-exit when candidate pool meets latency guard to reduce iterations. Required minor refactor before merge.
Jules Park (PM) (2026-03-07): Confirmed that customer-visible policy behavior must stay the same for Dedicated customers on contracts. Marked as high importance for rollout gating.

Sandeep Rao (SRE) (2026-03-12): Observed counter drift in simulator — recommended using monotonic counters with snapshotting during evaluation window. Filed ENG-47918 to centralize simulator counters.
Design review note (2026-03-06): Keep region affinity as a soft preference; do not hard-bind to region when capacity is low. This avoids cascading outages during zone degradation.
